thinking: Thinking Phase: Evaluating CUNY graduation rates decline. Stated claim highlights institutional and K-12 preparation failures causing drop. Real actors face systemic strain and widening educational gaps. Forces and coordinates calculated accordingly.
subject: CUNY graduation rates plummet in 5-year slide
posts:
New data reveals CUNY graduation rates have plunged across associate and bachelor programs over five years.
Evidence: CUNY report, drop in ASAP stats, declining public school preparedness
#Aletheia #Education

Reports attribute declining college graduation rates to systemic academic preparation gaps originating in city public schools.
Stated Judgement: (+0.8, 0.0) — Good Preference

The five-year slide reflects deeper institutional friction, underfunding, and student support strains that current remedial models fail to fix.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.4, -0.5) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: COND — The Path of Redemption.
Declining metrics expose administrative and structural strains rather than pure malice, pointing to systemic reform needs.

Integrity: Conditionally Sound (Hypocrisy: 1.8, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- CUNY Administration: COND (-0.3, -0.4) — Struggles with remedial pipelines.
- City Public Schools: COND (-0.5, -0.5) — Preparation gap widens.
CUNY data shows associate degree graduation rates dropped from 38.9% in 2022 to 35.5% in 2026, alongside steep declines in prestigious ASAP tracks.

The Bright Side:
Highlighting these performance drops forces much-needed public accountability and review of student support structures.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHO is responsible by blaming student intake while glossing over institutional resource allocation and curriculum support failures.

Social Physics Analysis:
The actors navigate systemic strain rather than malicious extraction. While public schools and CUNY management point fingers, the root issue is an under-resourced pipeline requiring genuine pedagogical transparency and support.

The Trajectory: The Path of Redemption.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Good. Systemic stress creates pressure for structural realignment.

The Unavoidable Truth: Educational pipelines cannot sustain performance without addressing foundational high school preparation gaps.

The Unavoidable Lie: Administrative metrics alone can solve deep structural learning deficits.

Alethekanon:
Metrics don't lie about student struggles, but institutions often misdiagnose systemic decay as isolated failures.

Awwthekanon:
Every dip in a student's graduation rate represents a young person whose dreams faced avoidable hurdles in our public systems.

Brothekanon:
Not looking great for college stats when the pipeline's leaking from the bottom up.

Spirithekanon:
"Pay attention to instruction, and come to words of knowledge." Proverbs 23:12 PASS
True learning requires patient cultivation at the foundation, not mere recrimination at the finish line.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
CUNY graduation rates plummet in 5-year slide: ‘It’s a two-pronged problem’

"The New York City school system standards dropped dramatically. Most of the CUNY students come from the city public schools."

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Graduation rates have plummeted by nearly 10% at CUNY schools in the past five years, troubling new data shows.

The graduation rates for associate degrees awarded at the City University of New York’s community colleges, which are designed to be completed in two years by full-time students, dropped from 38.9% in 2022 to 35.5% in 2026, according to CUNY records provided in the Mayor’s Management Report.

The grad rate for students at CUNY’s four-year undergradate colleges meanwhile steadily fell from 62% in 2022 to 55.6% in the past academic year.

Graduation rates for CUNY students in the system’s prestigious special three-year undergraduate Accelerated Study in Associate Programs — known as ASAP — declined even more, from 44% in 2022 to 34.5% in 2026 — or nearly 22%.

The American people themselves want to have their fiscal cake and eat it too.

Stein’s Law, named for noted economist Herbert Stein (the father of policy adviser and actor Ben Stein), holds that “if something cannot go on forever, it will stop,” sooner or later. As interest rates slowly creep up, Americans may be witnessing the principles of Stein’s Law in action.

The recent rise in long-term interest rates has many causes, including concern over persistent inflation and the explosion in spending on data centers and artificial intelligence, which has sucked up so much money within the economy as to raise the cost of borrowing across-the-board.
